scalesUsed.notes: Eb - F - G - Ab - Bb - C - D - Eb
scalesUsed.application: Forms the core harmonic canvas for the chorus (Ab - Bb - Eb - Cm) and Neil Finn's vocal melody

scalesUsed.notes: C - D - Eb - F - G - Ab - B - C
scalesUsed.application: Supplies the raised G major (V/vi) and E diminished/C7 secondary dominant tensions that give the verse its rich Beatlesque melancholy

keyAndScale.modalCharacter: Lush, chromatic pop sophistication blending Eb Ionian warmth with borrowed secondary dominants (C7 and G7) and suspended 4th embellishments
keyAndScale.relativeMinor: C minor is the relative minor of Eb major

mainProgression.progressionDescription: Neil Finn's signature jangle-pop verse cycle moving from a shimmering Ebmaj7/Eb tonic through C minor and Ab major before pivoting on a bittersweet G7 (V/vi) dominant.
mainProgression.description: Neil Finn's signature jangle-pop verse cycle moving from a shimmering Ebmaj7/Eb tonic through C minor and Ab major before pivoting on a bittersweet G7 (V/vi) dominant.

sectionProgressions.description: Dreamy 12/8-feel 4/4 sway using moveable barre voicings and colorful sus2/sus4 pinky extensions

sectionProgressions.progression: Ab - Bb - Eb - Cm - Ab - Bb - G7 - Cm
sectionProgressions.romanNumerals: IV - V - I - vi - IV - V - III7 - vi
sectionProgressions.description: Begins on the subdominant Ab before using G7 as a secondary dominant to pull poignantly into C minor on 'they come, they come'
Melodic double-stop and chord-tone soloing over the verse progression
Eb major triad and G7 chromatic third resolution exercise

harmonicFunction: Eb (I) - Warm tonic chord, frequently embellished as Ebadd9 or Ebsus2 at the 6th fret
Cm (vi) - Relative minor chord deepening the introspective mood
Ab (IV) - Subdominant chord launching the iconic 'Hey now, hey now' chorus
Bb (V) - Dominant chord resolving to Eb or setting up deceptive turns
G7 (III7 / V of vi) - Secondary dominant whose B natural creates an unforgettable bittersweet pull toward C minor

techniques.name: Embellished Barre Chords & Jangle-Pop Voice Leading
techniques.description: Neil Finn's hallmark technique of holding barre chord shapes around the 3rd to 6th frets while lifting and adding fingers to create shimmering sus2, sus4, and 7th extensions.

notes: Eb (A-shape barre): X-6-8-8-8-6 (or Ebsus2: X-6-8-8-6-6)
sequence: Establish the signature opening Ebsus2/Eb strum with a lazy, swung 16th-note lilt
Move smoothly from Eb to Cm and down to the 4th-fret Ab major barre chord
Slide your barre down one fret from Ab (fret 4) to G7 (fret 3) for effortless voice leading
In the chorus, emphasize the walkdown from Eb through D bass into Cm
tips: Want an easier open-chord version? Place a capo on the 3rd fret and play the entire song using C, Am, F, E7, and G shapes!
Let the high B and E strings ring through slight chorus and compressor effects for the authentic 1986 studio chime
Avoid stiff, robotic strumming—let your wrist swing with the soulful 82 BPM groove

techniques.name: Melodic Chord-Tone Phrasing & Chromatic Secondary Resolutions
techniques.description: Weaving singing single-note phrases around Mitchell Froom's Hammond organ solo, targeting the B-natural leading tone of G7 (V/vi) and connecting chord tones across the 3rd to 8th fret positions.

notes: Eb major triad tones (Eb, G, Bb) at frets 6 and 8
Targeting the chromatic B-natural (3rd string, 4th fret) over G7 to pull into Cm
Smooth finger vibrato and subtle pickup dynamics
Compressed clean tone with lush stereo chorus
sequence: Outline the Eb major triad on strings 1, 2, and 3
Shift to 8th position for the Cm chord tone response
Drop down to string 2 fret 6 over Ab
Land definitively on the B-natural on the 3rd string over the G7 secondary dominant
tips: Producer Mitchell Froom recorded his iconic Hammond solo alongside Neil's delicate guitar fills
Keep the touch feather-light with a thin-to-medium pick (0.60–0.73mm)
Use a subtle analog chorus like a Boss CE-2 to create the floating, liquid texture

sections.name: Intro Shimmer & Sus2 Hook
sections.description: Neil Finn's iconic opening motif toggling between Ebsus2 and Eb before setting the 82 BPM swung pop groove.
notes: Toggle pinky finger on the 2nd string between 6th (sus2) and 8th (major 3rd) frets
Keep right wrist loose with gentle 16th-note swing
Let the open, chimey high notes sustain

sections.name: Verse 1 Introspective Sway
sections.description: Neil Finn's introspective narrative ('There is freedom within, there is freedom without...') cycling through Eb, Cm, Ab, and G7.
notes: Toggle between Ebsus2 (X-6-8-8-6-6) and Eb (X-6-8-8-8-6) on the opening chord
Slide smoothly from Ab at the 4th fret to G7 at the 3rd fret
Let the B natural on G7 (3rd string 4th fret) sing clearly as the secondary dominant

sections.name: Pre-Chorus Tension & Build
sections.description: The harmonic lift building anticipation into the chorus hook, shifting energy from the melancholy verse into the soaring subdominant.
notes: Ascend cleanly from the 4th fret Ab to the 6th fret Bb
Hit the syncopated push into the Cm chord
Hold the final G7 chord before the chorus explosion

sections.name: Chorus Stadium Anthem ('Hey Now, Hey Now')
sections.description: The anthemic chorus starting on Ab and Bb before G7 redirects the resolution poignantly into C minor on 'they come, they come'.
sections.progression: Ab - Bb - Eb - Cm - Ab - Bb - G7 - Cm
notes: Climb from Ab (4th fret) to Bb (6th fret) to launch the chorus
Use the second half's G7 chord to create a poignant pull into Cm
Maintain warm, legato chord transitions with open top-string chime

sections.name: Melodic Guitar & Organ Interlude Solo
sections.description: The unforgettable instrumental interlude pairing Mitchell Froom's swirling Hammond organ with Neil Finn's lyrical, chord-conscious guitar lead.
notes: Play with a warm, singing tone and compressed clean sustain
Accentuate the high G (8th fret 1st string) over the Eb tonic
Target the B natural (3rd string, 4th fret) to outline the G7 turnaround perfectly

sections.name: Outro Chorus & Delicate Fade
sections.description: The delicate outro where the chorus cycles hypnotically while subtle arpeggiated guitar embellishments drift across the stereo panorama.
notes: Light arpeggio picking across the high triad strings
Dynamic decrescendo towards the final studio fade
Slight vibrato on high note sustains

guitar.pickup: Middle position (both pickups) for glassy 1980s jangle

amp.recommended: Roland JC-120 Jazz Chorus or Vox AC30

effects.distortion: None (clean preamp boost only for solo)
effects.other: Analog chorus pedal (Boss CE-2 style) and studio compressor

beginner.title: Capo 3 Open-Chord Arrangement
steps: Place a capo on the 3rd fret so Eb major becomes easy C major shapes (C - Am - F - E7)
Practice the verse progression (C - Am - F - E7) at 70 BPM
Learn the chorus (F - G - C - Am - F - G - E7 - Am) with smooth transitions
Strum along with the original recording at 82 BPM

intermediate.title: No-Capo Barre Chords & Sus Embellishments
steps: Play the authentic no-capo barre shapes in Eb major (Eb, Cm, Ab, G7, Bb)
Incorporate the Ebsus2 to Eb pinky movement in the intro and verse
Execute the Eb - Bb/D - Cm bass walkdown in the chorus

advanced.title: Chord-Melody Solo & Studio Nuances
steps: Learn the melodic guitar break weaving double-stops with Hammond organ lines
Add C7 and Edim7 passing voicings used in the late-verse variations
Master the swung 16th-note groove and dynamic touch

commonMistakes: Playing Gm instead of G7 in the verse and chorus—the B natural in G7 is the heart of the song
Fatiguing the fretting thumb by squeezing barre chords too hard
Strumming with a rigid straight-eighth feel instead of a relaxed 16th-note swing
practiceRoutine: 3 minutes: Ebsus2 to Eb barre chord finger-independence warmup at fret 6
5 minutes: Ab (fret 4) → G7 (fret 3) → Cm (fret 3) transition loop
5 minutes: Chorus walkdown and secondary dominant cadence at 82 BPM
focusAreas: Relaxed barre chord stamina in Eb major
Highlighting the III7 (G7) to vi (Cm) secondary dominant resolution
metronomeWork: Practice barre transitions at 68 BPM with zero string buzz
Set metronome to 82 BPM and subdivide into swung 16th notes
Focus on keeping time steady during the atmospheric instrumental break
